verdicts.evidence: Post overflow menu → `ReportPost.modal.tsx:180-196`: a 'Reply privately' CTA rendered only when `(userType === HOST || userType === SUPPORT) && userInfo.userType !== SUPPORT && post.actor !== userId` — i.e. host/support only, never to another support user, never to yourself. Its `replyPost` handler runs `usePostActions.ts:93-155`: `ExistsChannelCreated()` queries Stream for a `messaging` channel with members `[userId, post.actor]`; on miss it chains `createConnectionUser` → `AcceptConnection` → `client.channel('messaging', idChannel, {members, name: '<FirstName> Host'})`; then `sendMessageDirectly` captures the post view with `captureRef(...base64)`, fetches the group via `getGroupById`, and `navigation.replace(BuddiesScreen.Chat, {channelId, image, type:'ReplyHost', namePrivatly, dataGroup, post})`.
verdicts.note: Find-or-create is genuinely find-or-create: it reuses any existing 1:1 channel before minting a Connection record. The `captureRef` screenshot is presentation-only — web can attach the post object without rasterising it.

verdicts.evidence: `src/screens/feeds/activities-feed.tsx:34` declares `const MAX_EMPTY_RETRIES = 3`; the effect at :170-194 checks `hasFinishedLoading && hasPages && !hasPosts && emptyRetryCount.current < MAX_EMPTY_RETRIES`, increments the counter, sets `isRetrying`, and re-`mutate()`s after 1500ms, resetting the counter once posts arrive. `showLoadingIndicator = isValidating || isLoading || isRetrying` (:290-291) keeps the spinner up instead of flashing the empty state. Comment in source: 'This handles the intermittent issue where the Lambda returns empty on first call'.
verdicts.note: The same defence exists a second time in `src/screens/feeds/PostDetails.tsx:108-124` (one 1200ms re-fetch before believing a post is deleted) — same known Lambda intermittent, worth porting alongside. Pure backend-flakiness workaround; no product decision involved.

verdicts.evidence: Feeds tab → Discover (`FeedsRecomendedScreen` → `GroupsRecommended` → `GroupsRecommendedList`). Every row is a `GroupListItemLayout` whose `onSelect` calls `redirectToGroupDetails` (`GroupsRecommendedList.tsx:63-71`, invoked at :99-105 and :119-127), navigating to `FeedScreens.FeedDetail` with `{id, total, showButtons:true, idHost, isSecureGroup}`. That screen (`src/screens/feeds/group-details.tsx:103`) renders `GroupDetailsLayout`, which shows member count + View members (`GroupDetails.tsx:122-135`), ABOUT (:137-146), a HOSTED BY block with each host's avatar, occupation, pronoun, ambassador badge and bio (:148-178), and SPONSORED BY with the sponsor logo and description (:181-195) — with `ConnectionGroupLayout`'s JOIN button underneath.
verdicts.note: So on mobile the row is a link to a full pre-join detail screen and Join lives inside it; on web the row is a bare Join button. The presentation (screen vs. expanded sheet) is free — the missing capability is hosts + sponsor + member count + View members before joining.

What I saw: mobile fires `replyMessage` in exactly ONE place — `ChatMessagesInput.tsx:185-200`, inside `createNotification()`, and only on the ReplyHost chat send (`:154-166`). That path is already covered by `chat-context-entry-points`. It is never fired for a feed comment. Separately, `createGroupPost` (the AppSync mutation whose only purpose is to trigger the push/subscription) is fired exactly once, in `useFeedActivities.ts:43-53`, immediately after `feed.addActivity` — i.e. for POSTS only. Neither `addComment` nor `addThreadComment` (`useFeedReactions.ts:49-102`) fires any notification verb; they just POST a Stream reaction. Yet comment pushes clearly do arrive on mobile — `push-notification.provider.tsx:442-450` handles `msg.data.activityId` pushes as the 'group' kind. That means the comment→push trigger is server-side (most likely a Stream reaction webhook), not client-side. THE QUESTION FOR THE PRODUCT OWNER: does the backend already raise the comment push from a Stream reaction webhook — in which case web comments are notified for free and there is nothing to build — or does mobile get comment pushes through some path outside this repo that web must replicate? I will not guess, because building it wrong means web double-notifies on every comment.
verdicts.evidence: Reachability of the surface is not in doubt — Feeds tab → PostDetail → comment composer → `addComment` (`src/screens/feeds/PostDetails.tsx:290` → `useFeedReactions.ts:49-73`) is live. What is missing is any mobile client-side push trigger on that path: `grep -rn 'REPLYMESSAGE|replyMessage' src/` returns only `types/utils/lambda.ts:25` (the enum) and `ChatMessagesInput.tsx:189,192` (the ReplyHost chat send). `grep -rn 'createGroupPost' src/` returns only `hooks/feed/useFeedActivities.ts:12`, called at :43-53 after `addActivityUser`.

Requests tab (`RequestBuddiesNavigation` in `TabsScreens`) → `HomeRequestBuddies.tsx:158-166` renders `<ConnectionRequest connection={item} currentId={id} userInfo={userInfo} …/>` for each pending connection. `ConnectionRequest.tsx:58-67` calls `getLabelCoincidencies(Remitent.id, userInfo)` on mount and stores it; `:215` passes it as the card's `description={labelsCoincidence === null ? '...' : labelsCoincidence || ' '}` — the sender's bio is never rendered. `src/utils/coincidences.ts:26-95` re-fetches the sender via `GET_USER_USERS_DATA`, intersects Interests/Hospitals/Treatments/Diagnosis by id, and prefixes the sender's `State.name`, returning e.g. 'NY, Interests, Medical center'.
verdicts.note: The line names the CATEGORIES that overlap, not the individual values — `labelsAvatarDescripcion` maps the non-empty keys to labels. Note `HomeRequestBuddies.tsx:234` is a commented-out second `ConnectionRequest`; the live one is at :158.

verdicts.evidence: Two live flows both end in sign-out-and-return. Change status: Settings → Change status → `change-status-confirmation.tsx:44-58` — after `ChangeUserTypeService` succeeds it calls `signOut(setIsLoading)`, then `setUser(undefined); setUnEnrolledUser(undefined); setEmail(null)` and toasts. `ChangeStatusConfirmationLayout.tsx:44-66` does the same on the close button, with a source comment explaining the ordering: it switches to the Auth stack IMMEDIATELY 'because signOut makes flaky GetStream/GraphQL calls after Auth.signOut() that can hang forever and would otherwise strand the user on this screen'. Delete account: Settings → Delete account → `DeleteAccountSuccess.tsx:24,58` — both the X and 'GOT IT' call `setUser(null)`. `Main.tsx:80-84` keys the App-vs-Auth stack off `user`, so clearing it lands the member on a working signed-out screen.
verdicts.note: The load-bearing detail is the ordering: clear the session state FIRST, fire the backend sign-out cleanup in the background, and never let a hanging cleanup call block the redirect. Both mobile call sites do this deliberately.

verdicts.evidence: Updates tab (`TabsScreens` → `UpdatesNavigation` → `UpdatesScreens.tsx:11,22` → `HomeNotifications`) refetches on every foreground push: `HomeNotifications.tsx:139-141` is `useEffect(() => { refetch(); }, [hasPostMessage])`. The producer is `push-notification.provider.tsx:437-469`: `handleLocalNotification` appends to `hasPostMessage` on all three branches — chat/group pushes (`msg.data.channel || channelId || activityId`), `LIVE_NOTIFY`, and the generic connect branch — and the connect branch additionally calls `invalidateConnectionMap()` (:460) with the comment 'the cached connection statuses are now stale, so refresh them while the app is open'. The nav badge is driven from the same signal: `tab-bar.tsx:138-150` recomputes `notificationCount` from `hasPostMessage.length` and `hasVisitedNotificationsScreen`.
verdicts.note: So one push signal feeds three consumers on mobile: the Updates list refetch, the tab badge, and the connection-map invalidation. Web already has a live AppSync subscription for the requests tab only — the asymmetry the item describes is real.

verdicts.evidence: Enrollment event: `LoadingPersonalInformation.tsx:139-144` calls `setAnalyticsFlags()` then `emitEvent({event: localStorageAnalytics.bmcf_enrollment, eventParams:{timestamp: Date.now()}})` right after the user record is created; `src/analytics/events.ts:108-112` maps that to `analytics().logEvent('bmcf_enrollment', {timestamp})`. Login flags: `src/screens/signIn/Login/Login.tsx:41-57` defines `setAnalyticsFlags` writing 'true' to all five keys (chatWithFirstBuddy, connectWithFirstBuddy, joinFirstGroup, comment, post), and it is awaited on every successful sign-in at :68-72. `@react-native-firebase/analytics` is a real dependency (package.json:39).
verdicts.note: Behavioural detail the port must preserve: setting the five flags to 'true' on login SUPPRESSES the first-action events (events.ts:36-86 early-returns when the flag reads 'true'), so first-action events only ever fire for a session that just enrolled. That is mobile's semantics, odd as it looks — mirror it rather than 'fixing' it.

verdicts.evidence: Buddies tab → `Recommended.tsx:223-226` renders `<SearchBuddy/>`, whose 'SCAN QR' quick-search button (`SearchBuddy.tsx:116-120`) calls `handleNavigation('Scanner')` → `navigate(BuddiesScreen.QrIdentificationBuddies, {screen:'SCANQR'})` (`:29-33`), routed by `BuddiesScreens.tsx:142-143` to `QrIdentification`. With `params.screen === 'SCANQR'` that screen renders `<BuddyIdQr handleReadScanner showQr={false}/>` (`QrIdentification.tsx:70-73`), which mounts `<BuddyIdScanner/>` (`BuddyIdQr.tsx:59-70`). The scanner is a real `react-native-vision-camera` `useCodeScanner({codeTypes:['qr']})` with a camera-permission gate (`BuddyIdScanner.tsx:4,31-63`); `react-native-vision-camera` ^4.7.2 is in package.json:115. Decoded value flows into `handleReadScanner` (`QrIdentification.tsx:37-58`), which strips the deep-link prefix (`event.split('/').at(-1)` when the string contains LOCAL_DEEP_LINK/UNIVERSAL_DEEP_LINK) and hands the bare id to `getId` → `useValidateRules`, the SAME guard ladder the typed Buddy ID input uses.
verdicts.note: Note the package signal: `@mgcrea/vision-camera-barcode-scanner` is in package.json but imported nowhere — the live scanner uses vision-camera's own built-in `useCodeScanner`. Also, the QR entry point exists twice: 'SCAN QR' from Buddies discovery (above) and the 'Scan buddy's qr code' toggle on the own-QR screen reached from the hamburger header (`HamburgerHeader.tsx:69` → `BuddyIdQr.tsx:88-100`). Both are live.
